---
title: "The simulation: what the prior moves and what it does not"
subtitle: "Catalog A-06 and A-07"
description: "The paper's simulation in nine cells: the prior on alpha moves the posterior number of clusters, the collapse rate and the coverage of the true K, while the error of the site effects stays the same."
toc: false
---

The paper simulates multisite trials with J = 100 sites, a generating number of
components K* of 5, 10 or 30, and three levels of information I (how much each site's data say about its own
effect). Each cell is fitted 200 times under five priors on alpha.

```{=html}
<div id="w-simdash" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/sim-dashboard.js"></script>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), spec = {};
    if (q.get("preset")) spec.preset = q.get("preset");
    window.__dpxSim = DPX["sim-dashboard"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-simdash"), spec);
  })();
</script>
```

- **The number of clusters follows the prior.** At K* = 5 and I = .2 the posterior mean of K_J is
  1.50 under Vague and 3.41 under SSI-Weight, and the chance of a single cluster falls from .725
  to .315 (Dual-Anchor).
- **The site effects do not.** In every cell at I = .2 the RMSE of the site effects stays between
  .234 and .238, whatever the prior.
- **When the truth is far from the prior**, K* = 30, the SSI-Weight prior never covers it.

## The effects stay, the partition moves

```{=html}
<div id="w-evp" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/bundles/effects-vs-partition-tiles.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxEvp = DPX["effects-vs-partition-tiles"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-evp"), {});
</script>
```

- **Fixed lambda.** Holding the Dual-Anchor lambda at .16 (the selected value), .5 or .9 moves the
  posterior number of clusters from 2.47 to 1.76 to 1.54, and the RMSE by less than .001.
- **Unequal weights.** With one cluster holding 60% of the sites the pattern is the same: the RMSE
  is flat across priors, the collapse rate is not.

## When the elicited mean is wrong

The paper's misspecification grid states the target mean as r = mu_K / K* times the truth, with
r = .5, 1 or 2 (medium confidence, J = 100, grand-mean prior N(0, 100)).

```{=html}
<div id="w-misspec" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/bundles/misspecification.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxMis = DPX["misspecification"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-misspec"), {});
</script>
```

- **The posterior follows the elicited mean.** Under TSMM at K* = 10 and I = .2 the posterior mean
  of K_J moves from 1.51 to 3.41 to 15.03 as mu_K goes from 5 to 10 to 20.
- **Same mean, same answer.** The cells (K* = 5, r = 2) and (K* = 10, r = 1) share mu_K = 10 and
  both give 3.41, with collapse .391 in both, although the true counts differ by a factor of two.
  Switch the horizontal axis to mu_K and the trajectories for different K* fall on one curve.
- **The weight anchor matters only at small mu_K.** At mu_K = 5 (K* = 10, r = .5) Dual-Anchor
  raises the posterior mean from 1.51 to 2.48; from mu_K = 10 on, the trigger does not fire and
  Dual-Anchor coincides with TSMM.

## More sites do not fix the default

The design-size grid runs the same priors at J = 25, 50, 100 and 200 sites (K* = 5 or 10,
I = .2 or .8, grand-mean prior N(0, 100)).

```{=html}
<div id="w-design" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/bundles/design-size.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxDes = DPX["design-size"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-design"), {});
</script>
```

- **The default stays collapsed.** Under Vague the posterior mean of K_J stays between 1.18 and
  1.46 and the collapse probability is at least .765 even at J = 200.
- **Dual-Anchor moves toward the reference count.** At K* = 5 and I = .2 its posterior mean goes
  from 1.53 at J = 25 to 3.50 at J = 200 (collapse .716 to .271) while TSMM stays near 1.5; the
  selected lambda changes from .70 to .30, .16 and .09 along the way, so this is a policy
  trajectory, not a sample-size effect alone.
- **SSI-Weight ignores the design.** Its trajectories are the same at K* = 5 and K* = 10
  (2.17 to 2.99 and 2.16 to 2.99 at I = .2), with collapse near .5.
- At I = .8 and J = 200 only 30 to 93 of 200 fits pass the diagnostics; those points are hollow.
